chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad from Ibn Sama'ah from Abdullah ibn Jabala from Ali ibn Abi Hamza from Abu Baseer from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'Then appoint a judge from his family and a judge from her family.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The two judges stipulate: If they wish, they separate [the couple], and if they wish, they gather [them]. So if they gather them, it is valid, and if they separate them, it is valid.'

key_terms.أَهْلُهُ: His family (referring to the husband's family)
key_terms.أَهْلِهَا: Her family (referring to the wife's family)
key_terms.حَكَمٌ: Arbitrator or judge appointed to resolve a dispute
key_terms.يَشْتَرِطَانِ: They stipulate or agree upon terms

ai.seo_question: What is the role and authority of the two arbitrators in resolving marital disputes according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the procedural discretion of the two arbitrators (hakam) appointed for marital discord, affirming that both reconciliation and separation are legally valid outcomes based on their mutual agreement. It underscores the flexibility in Islamic jurisprudence, allowing the arbitrators to either keep the couple together or separate them, reflecting the practical application of Quranic guidance on resolving family disputes.
